newsitem.title: UK: Zinc contango edges out on LME, still narrow.
newsitem.headline: Zinc contango edges out on LME, still narrow.

text.p: The contango for cash/threes zinc on the London Metal Exchange (LME) edged out from Friday's levels of $1/3 a tonne, but still remained tight at around $5 on Monday.
Zinc's contango has contracted steadily from levels of $24 prevailing in mid-June, while the market has leapt to the highest levels for nearly seven years on the LME.
Traders said a net 1,875-tonne LME warehouse stock increase on Monday, incorporating 2,750 tonnes delivered into Singapore, helped allay some concerns over Chinese metal quality.
There had been talk recently that much of the metal being delivered from China into Singapore was old and of doubtful quality.
However, earlier on Monday China's Zhuzhou smelter said that Swiss trader Glencore, which had been querying the quality of its 'TORCH' brand, had withdrawn a complaint made to the LME.
Neither Glencore or the LME were available for comment.

Traders for some time have expected a sizeable tonnage of metal from China, perhaps up to 40,000 tonnes, to be delivered into Singapore. But its non-appearance in data suggested that the metal was being held off-warrant.
As of today, there are 31,750 tonnes of zinc in Singapore, against some 10,000 tonnes in mid-April.

Some traders said the talk of complaints was part of a wider game between major longs and shorts. In the latter case some say there is a large Chinese investment position now some $200 to $300 under the current market price of $1,420, they said.

In the long run, analysts expect Chinese zinc exports to remain well above 1996 levels. Exports of zinc and zinc alloys from China in the first five months of this year were 198,386 tonnes, against a 1996 overall total of 226,777 tonnes.
Macquarie Equities Ltd said there would be slow-down, as the rainy season in China normally causes mine and smelter production to slow.
But it still expects exports of 400,000 tonnes this year, which could lead to a downward correction in zinc prices in the summer months.
